newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Gazprom shifts payments to Hungary unit.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom shifts payments to Hungary unit.

text.p: Gazprom's Hungarian banking arm, Altalanos Ertekforgalmi Bank (AEB), has taken over accounting for payments for the Russian group's gas shipments to the Czech Republic and Austria, the bank said on Thursday.
The payments amount to some $100 million every month.
AEB, owned by Gazprombank, said in a statement that Gazprom also planned to shift to AEB payments on gas shipments to other European countries.
"This is an important factor in increasing activity and profitability," AEB said.

"According to the projection of the bank's managers -- maintaining the dynamic pace of development in the past almost one year -- AEB will become one of the largest banks in Hungary by about the year 2000," it added.

AEB said that Gazprombank raised its registered capital to five billion forints ($26.5 million) to 9.8 billion forints in March and the owner planned to boost that amount to 25 billion forints by the end of 1997.
The bank almost doubled its balance sheet total to 71.6 billion forints in 1996 and plans to boost it to above 130 billion forints this year, AEB said.

The bank posted a pre-tax profit of 188 million forints last year, while the pre-tax profit in the first half of this year was up at 1.56 billion forints and is likely to rise to about three billion forints by the end of 1997, the bank added.
-- Sandor Peto, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040 ($ = 188.4 Hungarian Forints)
